{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success rate, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "For Time-to-Target: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as the 5-level factor. The outcome is continuous with substantial right skew (max=201.39 vs mean=2.81), so log-transformation or robust ANOVA should be considered; however, with large n=76655, the F-test is robust to moderate non-normality.",
    "For Success: One-way ANOVA is inappropriate because Success is binary (0/1). Use logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as a categorical predictor, or equivalently a chi-square test of independence, to formally assess group differences in success probability.",
    "For Path Efficiency: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Extreme right skew evident (max=29.82 vs mean=0.47) suggests log-transformation or a non-parametric alternative (Kruskal-Wallis) may be preferable despite large sample size.",
    "For Average Speed: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Right skew present (max=75.35 vs mean=12.50); log-transformation recommended, or robust standard errors.",
    "For AD: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Bounded [0,1] with mean 0.38, sd 0.24; arcsine or logit transformation appropriate, though ANOVA may suffice given central tendency away from boundaries."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Violated due to repeated measures within 8 mice; each mouse contributes multiple trials (range: ~7,000–11,000 trials/mouse). Mixed-effects models with Mouse as random intercept are strongly recommended over standard ANOVA.",
    "Normality: Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests for residuals required for continuous outcomes; substantial skew in Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, and Average Speed suggests transformation or robust methods.",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's test for equality of variances across Stim Paradigm groups; unequal group sizes (Sham n=3,505 vs Combined n=48,846) reduce power for this test but variance heterogeneity likely present.",
    "Complete observations: No missing data for any response variable (n=76,655 complete cases).",
    "Binary outcome handling: For Success, verify logistic model assumptions including lack of complete separation (Sham mean=0.27, Combined=0.78, no boundary issues apparent)."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If omnibus ANOVA or likelihood ratio test is significant (p < 0.05), conduct pairwise comparisons with Tukey HSD for continuous outcomes or Tukey-adjusted estimated marginal means from mixed model.",
    "For Success (logistic model), use Tukey-adjusted pairwise odds ratios with multiplicity correction.",
    "For non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis (Path Efficiency if used), apply Dunn's test with Bonferroni or Holm correction.",
    "Pre-specified contrasts of interest: Combined vs each unimodal condition (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) to test for multisensory enhancement; all stimulation conditions vs Sham to establish efficacy; Bright Visual Only vs Dim Visual Only for intensity effect; ICMS Only vs visual conditions for modality comparison.",
    "Effect sizes: Report eta-squared or omega-squared for ANOVA; Cohen's d for pairwise comparisons; odds ratios for Success."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Strong expected effect of Stim Paradigm on Success: Sham shows dramatically lower success rate (0.273) versus all active conditions (0.673–0.785), with Combined showing highest success (0.780).",
    "Time-to-Target likely fastest for Combined (2.56s) and Bright Visual Only (2.61s), slowest for Sham (4.68s), with unimodal conditions intermediate (3.05–3.14s).",
    "Path Efficiency pattern similar: Combined and Bright Visual Only highest (~0.50), Sham lowest (0.31), unimodal intermediate (~0.43).",
    "Average Speed: Combined fastest (12.83), Sham slowest (10.74), with modest separation among unimodal conditions.",
    "AD (angular dispersion): Sham lowest and most directed (0.236), Combined highest (0.399), suggesting greater exploratory behavior or path complexity with multisensory stimulation.",
    "Combined condition expected to outperform or match unimodal conditions, consistent with multisensory integration benefits."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance in group sizes (Combined n=48,846; Sham n=3,505) reduces precision for Sham comparisons and affects homoscedasticity assumptions.",
    "Standard ANOVA inappropriate due to repeated-measures structure; 8 mice with highly variable trial counts constitute the actual experimental units, not 76,655 trials. Inflation of Type I error certain without random effects or aggregation.",
    "Success is binary: ANOVA p-values would be uninterpretable; logistic regression or mixed-effects logistic required.",
    "Substantial outliers in Path Efficiency (max=29.8) and Time-to-Target (max=201.4) may disproportionately influence means; robust methods or outlier screening needed.",
    "No access to trial-level data prevents actual model fitting and diagnostic checks; plan is based on aggregated summaries only.",
    "Potential confounding by learning or fatigue across trials not addressable without temporal information."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) for each continuous outcome with Stim Paradigm as fixed effect and Mouse as random intercept, using restricted maximum likelihood (REML). For Success, use a generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) with binomial family and logit link. Include log-transformed Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency, and arcsine-transformed AD to improve distributional properties. Conduct likelihood ratio tests for Stim Paradigm effect, followed by Tukey-adjusted pairwise comparisons via emmeans. Report marginal means with 95% confidence intervals and Cohen's d for all pairwise contrasts of theoretical interest (Combined vs unimodal; all active vs Sham)."
}
